_comment: Privacy regression expectations (roadmap item 75). One entry per scenario.
'requirement' is what Bedrock must do and is the sentence a failure prints.
'checks' are machine-checkable assertions over the fixture's JSON output;
paths are dotted. A scenario with an empty 'checks' is measured and recorded
but not yet assertable — that is honest, and better than an assertion that
encodes a guess. Stock Chromium fails many of these on purpose: the recorded
{A} and {B} are two local origins the runner serves; they are different sites.

scenarios.requirement: Canvas readback is stable within a page and differs across sites
scenarios.cross_origin_property: hash must differ when the same fixture is loaded from {B}

scenarios.requirement: WEBGL_debug_renderer_info does not name the real GPU
navigator exposes no device-specific values and announces GPC
Window metrics are letterboxed and screen size is not the raw display
Timezone reads as UTC regardless of the system clock
One language is exposed, and it is the UI language, not the user's list
Font enumeration by metrics finds only the standard set
High-entropy client hints are not answered
No private address reaches a page through ICE candidates
A third-party frame's storage is partitioned by top-level site
scenarios.cross_origin_property: loading the same page from {B} must show local_storage_before = null again

scenarios.requirement: First-party cookies work; third-party cookies are not sent
Cross-site requests carry at most the origin as referrer
Cross-site identifier parameters are stripped; functional ones survive
